title: Claude's Advertising Strategy: Every Meta, LinkedIn and Google Ad
summary: How Anthropic advertises Claude: 379 creator ads with #claudepartner and personal clau.de links, 42 Google task pages, LinkedIn campaigns aimed at open opportunities.
body_markdown:
Anthropic's ads run on three rails that never touch.


A creator program with its own hashtag and its own short links. A Google account that builds a landing page for every task someone searches. And a B2B machine on LinkedIn whose campaign names say exactly which accounts it's chasing.


Almost none of it carries a tracking tag. 53 of 1,211 Meta ads have a UTM. The attribution lives in the link itself.


It lines up with what companies buy. In Ramp's October 2026 AI category data, Claude Code is the most-purchased coding agent, bought by 87% of buyers in the category, and Anthropic is the most-purchased foundational LLM vendor at 80%.


## Claude ads: key findings


- **1,211** Meta ads since February 2026, **528** live; **832** from Claude's page, **379** from **84** creator pages
- **297** creator ads carry #claudepartner, **45** say "sponsored by Anthropic"
- Five creators get a personal clau.de short link: clau.de/maddy, clau.de/ux, clau.de/dawn, clau.de/majavoje, clau.de/stevehuynh
- Only **53** of 1,211 Meta ads carry a UTM tag
- **270** Google ads go to **42** task pages: /ai/marketing, /ai/file-organizer, /excel/formula-fix. Ten tasks have two versions, /ai/ and /cowork/
- LinkedIn campaign names target named accounts, open opportunities and Dun & Bradstreet industries: \[B2B_CL1P_EVG_T1\]-US_LI_ACC_TEXEC_OPPS_IMG_EBOOKS
- **478** Meta ads go to Claude Code, **260** to Cowork. Live, creators run **59** of the **88** Cowork ads
- **378** of 379 creator ads have no headline; every one is a video
- The median ended ad ran **15 days**


## How Claude pays creators


84 creator pages have run 379 Meta ads for Claude. 97 are live.


The deal is visible in the copy. 297 of the 379 carry #claudepartner. 77 carry #ad. 45 say it in words: "This video is sponsored by Anthropic." That's a paid partnership program with one hashtag across all of it, and the ads run from the creators' own pages, so Anthropic is paying for the post and for the media behind it.


### The short links


A few creators get something more: a personal link on Anthropic's own short domain.


Link Creator Where


clau.de/maddy Cyb3rmaddy Meta, 12 ads


clau.de/ux Aneta Kmiecik Meta, 6 ads


clau.de/dawn Dawn Choo LinkedIn, 4 ads


clau.de/majavoje Maja Voje LinkedIn, 4 ads


clau.de/stevehuynh Steve Huynh LinkedIn, 1 ad


One slug per creator, on a domain Anthropic owns. Every click is counted per creator without a single tag in the ad. That is how a creator program gets measured when 1,158 of 1,211 Meta ads carry no UTM at all.


No public creator rate turned up, and no open affiliate program for individuals. The cash that is public goes to students: campus ambassadors get a $3,600 stipend for the year, across three tracks, undergrad builder clubs, grad conversations and PhD science workshops. City community ambassadors get event funding and API credits, and the program says outright it doesn't include payment. Consultancies get referral credit through the partner network. The creator money stays private.


### Creators carry Cowork


Source Ads To Claude Code To Cowork Live Cowork


Claude page 832 342 123 29


Creator pages (84) 379 173 165 59


Claude's own page sells Claude Code, 342 ads against 123 for Cowork. The creators split it nearly even. Live today, creators run 59 of the 88 Cowork ads, but only 30 of the 241 live Claude Code ads. In September they made 56 of the 59 new Cowork ads.


The faces are not engineers. Natalie Barbu builds a CEO dashboard "without writing a single line of code". Corporate Natalie and Corporate Bro show Cowork doing weekly round-ups. nickbilotto built a surf forecast. On LinkedIn the creators are B2B voices with their own short links: Dawn Choo on data, Maja Voje on go-to-market.


**Corporate Natalie.** Cowork, for the workday. **Coding with Lewis.** A robot arm and a coffee shop. **The PM lander.** Claude Code for product managers.


**Measure creators with links, not tags.** A short link per creator on your own domain survives every repost, screenshot and caption edit. A UTM doesn't.


## How Claude's funnel is wired


### Google builds a page for every task


270 Google ads go to 42 task pages. The headline is the search term: "AI marketing agent - Claude by Anthropic", "AI file organizer", "AI presentation maker".


Page family Examples


/ai/<task> /ai/research, /ai/marketing, /ai/sales, /ai/finance, /ai/legal, /ai/slides, /ai/file-organizer


/cowork/<task> /cowork/research, /cowork/marketing, /cowork/sales, /cowork/slides


/excel/<problem> /excel/formula-fix, /excel/error-fix, /excel/data-analysis


/lp/cowork-for-<team> /lp/cowork-for-legal, /lp/cowork-for-marketing


Ten tasks exist twice: /ai/marketing and /cowork/marketing, /ai/slides and /cowork/slides. Same query, two page templates. One even carries a slug written by a machine: /ai/ai--agent. This is a page per search term, built at scale, with the template under test.


The Excel pages are the sharpest. Nobody searches "AI agent". People search for why their formula broke.


### Three Google accounts, three jobs


Account Variations What it sells


Main 1,719 Products by name: Claude Code, Cowork, Tag, the task pages


Second 167 Curiosity, all video, US: "What does AI know about me?", "Iceland's national pivot to AI"


Third 10 One film: "There's hope in hard questions"


Performance, education and brand never share a budget line. The second account sends people to academy.claude.com, Anthropic's AI literacy courses. It's selling trust in AI before it sells Claude.


### LinkedIn says which accounts it wants


The LinkedIn campaign names are a targeting spec:


Campaign Read it as


\[B2B_CL1P_EVG_T1\]-EMEA_LI_CNSD_TEXEC_DNBINDUSTRY_IMG_CASESTUDIES Evergreen, tier 1, EMEA, consideration, tech execs, Dun & Bradstreet industry segments, case studies


\[B2B_CL1P_EVG_T1\]-US_LI_ACC_TEXEC_OPPS_IMG_EBOOKS US, account list, tech execs at accounts with open opportunities, ebooks


\[B2B_CL1P_EVG_T1\]-EMEA_LI_ACC_TEXEC_OPPST1_IMG_EBOOKS Same in EMEA, opportunity stage 1


\[B2B_CL1P_EVG_T1\]-LI_US_LEADGEN_ACC Lead gen forms to an account list


baw_cl1p_emea_opus46 Brand awareness, EMEA, a model launch


OPPS means accounts that are already open deals in the CRM. The ads land on case studies (Coinbase, Rakuten, Brex, Snowflake) and an enterprise ebook. Sales has a deal open, and marketing follows the buying committee around LinkedIn with proof.


Where the targeting is readable, it leans Europe: 57 ads say "EMEA, Europe", 14 "EMEA", 12 "Germany, France and the United Kingdom".


**Put the CRM stage in the campaign name.** An ad that only runs to open opportunities is a sales tool, and naming it that way keeps it out of the brand budget.


## Where the Meta clicks go


Destination Ads What it is


claude.com/product/claude-code 478 Claude Code


claude.com/product/cowork 260 Cowork, the desktop agent for knowledge work


claude.ai 108 Straight into the app


claude.com/product/overview 95 Product overview


claude.com/problem-solvers 70 Customer docuseries


claude.com/product/claude-code/pm-v1 37 Claude Code, for product managers


claude.com/product/tag 36 Claude inside Slack


anthropic.com/claude/fable 19 Fable 5.1 launch


claude.com/lp/cowork-for-data 15 Cowork, for data teams


Claude Code gets 515 ads with the PM page. The model launches get a sliver: 19 for Fable 5.1, 12 for Sonnet 5.5. A frontier lab, and its Meta account mostly ignores the model race.


The ramp was June. 84 new ads in May, 322 in June, then 112, 151, 208. Cowork went from 39 new ads in May to 94 in June and 59 in September.


### The video carries the message


378 of the 379 creator ads have no headline. Every one is a video with a first-person caption. The brand ads run the other way: 404 of 832 have a headline, and 506 have no body text at all. "Try Claude Code" heads 72, "Try Claude Cowork" 49.


**Cowork.** "Takes on the work between the work." **The Problem Solvers.** "For founders changing the code."


### The customer docuseries


"The Problem Solvers" runs 70 Meta ads, 68 live, each a founder named in the copy: Anton Osika of Lovable in 20, Max Junestrand in 17, Kay Zhu in 8, Scott Wu in 8, Cursor in 7. On Google it runs as headlines: "Genspark: The Problem Solvers", "Cognition: The Problem Solvers". Customer proof, aimed at the buyer already shopping for a coding agent.


## How long an ad lives


683 ads have ended. The median ran 15 days. 316 were gone within two weeks, and only 17 ran past 60. The median live ad is 19 days old and the oldest has run since 18 June.


That's a two-week rotation with a small evergreen core.


## What actually makes this work


Each rail is measured its own way. Creators by their own short link. Search by a page per task. LinkedIn by the stage of the deal. No rail needs the others to report.


And the creators go where the brand page doesn't. A CEO or a corporate creator won't watch a lab explain a terminal. They'll watch someone like them do their job with it.
